cards.explanation: The answer is False. God says, “As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, you will no longer quote this proverb in Israel.” (Ezekiel 18:3) He puts His own life behind those words. The sour grapes saying is finished, friends.

The answer is God Himself. He says, “…every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine.” (Ezekiel 18:4) So the souls in this story were never anybody else's to trade around, friends. They're His.
The answer is "own." God says, “The soul who sins is the one who will die.” (Ezekiel 18:4) Each soul answers for its own sin, friends. That's the opposite of the sour grapes saying.

The answer is "need." The righteous man “…gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.” (Ezekiel 18:7) He sees people in need and he hands over what he has. Bread and clothing are just part of how he lives, bakers, because God's list goes on.

The answer is True. God says of the righteous man, “That man is righteous; surely he will live, declares the Lord GOD.” (Ezekiel 18:9) He follows God's statutes and faithfully keeps His ordinances. And God says he will live, friends.

The answer is False. God asks about the violent son, “Will this son live? He will not!” (Ezekiel 18:13) The text ties his death to “…all these abominations…” his own, and nothing about his father's goodness changes that. His father's righteous life doesn't carry him, friends.

The answer is that he thinks it over and does not copy it. He “…sees all the sins his father has committed, considers them, and does not do likewise…” (Ezekiel 18:14) He looks, he thinks, and he walks a different way. A front-row seat doesn't mean he has to join the show, bakers.

The answer is True. God says of the father, “…he will die for his own iniquity, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what was wrong among his people.” (Ezekiel 18:18) The son's good choices belong to the son, friends. Each one stands on his own.

The answer is that he did what is just and right. God says, “Since the son has done what is just and right, carefully observing all My statutes, he will surely live.” (Ezekiel 18:19) His life is tied to what he did, friends. Nothing about it depends on his father.

The answer is the one who did it. “The righteousness of the righteous man will fall upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked man will fall upon him.” (Ezekiel 18:20) It lands on the one who did it, and on nobody else, bakers. That's why a son isn't stuck with his father's sin.

The answer is False, and that is a lot of good news, friends. God says, “…he will surely live; he will not die.” (Ezekiel 18:21) “None of the transgressions he has committed will be held against him.” (Ezekiel 18:22) When he turns, his past isn't held against him.

The answer is that he turns from his ways and lives. That's God's own heart on the matter, friends. He asks, “Wouldn’t I prefer that he turn from his ways and live?” (Ezekiel 18:23) He asks it right after asking if He takes any pleasure in the death of the wicked. The answer He's pointing to is no.

The answer is that none of them will be remembered. God says, “None of the righteous acts he did will be remembered.” (Ezekiel 18:24) Turning away to the same abominations as the wicked takes a man's past good deeds off the table. It's a sobering verse, friends, and I think it's a loving warning to keep going.

The answer is False. God asks, “…will he live?” and gives the answer: “Because of the unfaithfulness and sin he has committed, he will die.” (Ezekiel 18:24) Turning to the abominations of the wicked is what costs him. A good start doesn't cover a turn like that, bakers.

The answer is True. The people say, “The way of the Lord is not just.” God answers, “Is it My way that is unjust? Is it not your ways that are unjust?” (Ezekiel 18:25) He hands the question right back to them, friends. It's like handing someone the mirror.

The answer is each according to his ways. God says, “…I will judge you, each according to his ways…” (Ezekiel 18:30) One person at a time, by what they did. It matches everything we just heard, friends.

The answer is so their iniquity won't be their downfall. God says, “Repent and turn from all your transgressions, so that your iniquity will not become your downfall.” (Ezekiel 18:30) The call to turn comes with a reason, and the reason is that they don't fall. I think that's a Father pointing out the open door, bakers.

The answer is to cast them away. God says, “Cast away from yourselves all the transgressions you have committed…” (Ezekiel 18:31) Throw them out, every last one. Think of sweeping crumbs off the counter instead of saving them for later, friends.
